In July 2014 there was a total of 641.6 million internet users in China. Over the previous years the rate had risen by rates ranging from 4-19%, with smaller values tending to be more recent. Increases are likely to continue. The Chinese government is probing to see what the current rate of internet access in China is. The motivations behind this are unclear; obviously greater internet access will be an improvement to China, but cynical groups believe this may indicate a new round of censorship legislation.

[M]

We need to model 2014-2015, as well as 2015-2016, 2016-2017, 2017-2018, and 2018-2019 in setting.

For 2014-2015, I would recommend 2% + 1d8 % growth, which would capture a range of recent values.

As time has gone on the ability to grow will decrease as it nears 100%, but increasing economy will be pushing this up. I’ll assume for now that these forces are leveling each other off. As such, for 2015-2016, 2016-2017 and 2017-2018 I propose the same roll as 2014-2015: 2% + 1d8% growth.

However, with the massive success in the liberalization of agriculture, the 300 million agricultural workers in China have seen some of China’s poorest citizens acquiring an amount of wealth, and possibly internet access. Since such a huge population has opened up to access, I would say it be 8% + 1d12% for 2018-2019, not to repeat again.

So, a d8 for 2014-2015, 2015-2016, 2016-2017, and 2017-2018, and a d12 for 2018-2019.
